newsitem.title: FINLAND: MINISTER AURA SAYS LIKES PRIVATE ROAD FINANCING.
newsitem.headline: MINISTER AURA SAYS LIKES PRIVATE ROAD FINANCING.

text.p: Finland's new transport minister Matti Aura said on Thursday that private-sector financing of infrastructure investments like highways should continue.
"The successful use of new forms of financing (transport sector infrastructure project) should be continued," Aura said in a statement released with his first news conference as cabinet minister.
Aura noted that the five-party left-right-green government coalition's programme stated that the transport sector infrastructure should be kept in shape.
"The current road and railway networks and other transport infrastructure must under no circumstances be allowed to fall into decay," he said.
Turning to telecommunications, another area governed by the transport ministry, Aura said: "The policy of liberalising the telecoms markets and competition will be continued."
Finland was already a forerunner in the liberalisation of the telecoms sector, he said.

Thanks to the liberalisation which had already taken place; "The competitive home market has built the foundation for the rise of the electronics industry into Finland's quickest growing export industry sector," Aura said.

The transport ministry was also involved in national and European projects targetted at turning Finland into an information society, he said. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
